answer:
Momentum SGD keeps an exponentially decayed gradient sum. AdamW keeps first and second moments, corrects their initialization bias, and applies parameter decay outside those moments. State is owned by torch.optim.Optimizer so state_dict works normally. Parameters without gradients are skipped. These implementations support dense gradients and closures but omit performance options such as fused/foreach updates.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Adam maintains $m_t=\beta_1m_{t-1}+(1-\beta_1)g_t$ and $v_t=\beta_2v_{t-1}+(1-\beta_2)g_t^2$, then uses bias-corrected moments. AdamW applies a separate shrinkage factor approximately $1-\eta\lambda$. Adding L2 gradients before adaptive normalization is generally different because coordinate-wise preconditioning also rescales that penalty. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05101)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://www.fast.ai/posts/2018-07-02-adam-weight-decay.html) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html).
